questions.question: What did we cover in the Delacroix migration outline?
questions.answer: Discovery, catalogue cleanup, Shopify configuration, integrations, testing, launch, and post-launch support, as a separate proposal workstream.
questions.quote: I drafted a six-week Delacroix Cosmetics migration outline, from discovery and catalogue cleanup through Shopify configuration, integrations, testing, launch, and post-launch support. I’ve kept it as a separate proposal workstream.

questions.question: What did we cover in the final Marchetti refund review?
questions.answer: Removing the duplicate refund adjustment, calculating VAT from the post-refund taxable net, regression coverage for sale-plus-refund totals and the PDF VAT line, coverage for multiple refunds and ordinary invoices, and the remaining mixed-VAT-rate refund risk.
questions.quote: The final diff removes the duplicate refund adjustment and calculates VAT from the post-refund taxable net. Regression coverage now checks sale-plus-refund totals and the PDF VAT line, while the full suite covers multiple refunds and ordinary invoices. The remaining risk is unusual mixed VAT-rate refunds, which are not represented in the current fixtures.

questions.question: What did I say the Orbit PATCH limiter had to return?
questions.answer: A 429 response with the standard rate-limit headers and Retry-After, without affecting other routes.
questions.quote: Return 429 with the standard rate-limit headers and Retry-After, and don’t affect other routes. Then show me the changed files.

questions.question: What did we conclude was the main Huang query bottleneck?
questions.answer: Scanning the large ledger_entries table and repeatedly joining it to accounts without a useful index on the join and date-filter columns.
questions.quote: Most of the runtime is spent scanning the large ledger_entries table and repeatedly joining it to accounts without a useful index on the join and date-filter columns. I’ve identified the expensive plan nodes and have not changed the database.

questions.question: What did I say had to be checked on the Marchetti sample PDF?
questions.answer: The invoice lines, subtotal, refund, VAT, and final total had to be inspected for internal consistency.
questions.quote: Generate a sample PDF from the regression fixture and inspect the invoice lines, subtotal, refund, VAT, and final total. Don’t change anything yet; tell me whether the displayed amounts are internally consistent.

questions.question: What exact limit and window did we set for Orbit PATCH requests?
questions.answer: 30 requests per minute per authenticated user.
questions.quote: I implemented the authenticated-user rate limiter only on PATCH /users/:id, after authentication and before the handler. It allows 30 requests per minute and returns 429 with rate-limit and Retry-After headers when exceeded.

questions.question: What exact Marchetti full-refund values did we use?
questions.answer: A €100 sale with a €100 refund had to produce a €0 net total.
questions.quote: I added one focused test asserting that a €100 sale with a €100 refund produces a €0 net total; the full invoice suite still passes.

questions.question: What execution-time improvement did the Huang join rewrite produce?
questions.answer: It improved execution from about 8 seconds to roughly 3 seconds.
questions.quote: The plan avoids the repeated join work and improves execution from about 8 seconds to roughly 3 seconds with the new index. Production was not touched.

questions.question: What did we reject about the original Marchetti refund calculation, why, and what replaced it?
questions.answer: We rejected subtracting the €10 refund both during CSV normalization and aggregation because it produced €80 instead of €90; the duplicate adjustment was to be removed.
questions.quote: The fixture produces a net total of €80 instead of the expected €90: the €10 refund is subtracted once while normalizing CSV rows and again when invoice totals are aggregated. I’ve traced both code paths and can now remove the duplicate adjustment.

questions.question: What did we reject about the Huang join, why, and what replaced it?
questions.answer: We rejected repeatedly joining raw filtered ledger entries to accounts because it caused unnecessary repeated work; it was replaced by aggregating the filtered ledger entries before the join.
questions.quote: I rewrote the join to aggregate the filtered ledger entries before joining to accounts, then ran EXPLAIN ANALYZE locally. The plan avoids the repeated join work and improves execution from about 8 seconds to roughly 3 seconds with the new index.

questions.question: Was it me or the agent who picked the Huang composite-index column order?
questions.quote: I recommend a composite index on ledger_entries (account_id, posted_at): account_id supports the join and posted_at narrows each account’s rows by date. I have not created it.

questions.question: Was it me or the agent who required the Codex approval change to stay repo-only?
questions.quote: Quick Codex CLI question before I continue: on Windows, how can I stop it asking for approval on every shell command in this repo only? I don’t want to weaken the setting globally.
